'''UltraTech Cement Limited''' is an Indian multinational cement company based in [[Mumbai]]. It is the largest manufacturer of grey cement, [[ready-mix concrete]] (RMC) and white cement in India, and the fifth largest in the world, with an installed capacity of 152.70 million tonnes per annum and 119 million tonnes per annum sales volume.<ref>{{Cite web|url=https://www.financialexpress.com/business/industry-ultratech-cement-acquires-cement-grinding-assets-of-burnpur-cement-for-rs-169-79-crore-3321051/|title=Ultratech Acquires cement grinding assets of burnpur cement|date=29 November 2023 }}</ref><ref>{{Cite web|url=https://www.grasim.com/Upload/PDF/utcl-financials-fy24.pdf|title=Ultratech Annual Report 2024}}</ref>

== History ==
UltraTech Cement traces its origins to 1983 when it began as the cement division of [[Larsen & Toubro]] (L&T), being sold under the "L&T Cement" brand. In 2000, L&T decided to sell its cement business and incorporated a wholly owned subsidiary to house the cement assets.<ref>{{cite news |title=L & T Cement Bidders May Be Losing Interest |url=https://www.business-standard.com/article/specials/l-t-cement-bidders-may-be-losing-interest-100093001024_1.html |access-date=8 May 2024 |work=Business Standard}}</ref>

In 2001, [[Reliance Industries]] sold its entire 10% stake in L&T to [[Grasim Industries]]. At the time, L&T was the largest cement manufacturer in India, while Grasim was the third-largest.<ref>{{cite news |title=Reliance sells 10 per cent stake in L&T to Grasim: Reuters |url=https://www.rediff.com/money/2001/nov/19l&t.htm |access-date=8 May 2024 |work=Rediff}}</ref><ref>{{cite news |title=India: Cement industry taking a concrete shape |url=https://www.arabnews.com/node/216869 |access-date=8 May 2024 |work=Arab News |date=10 December 2001 |language=en}}</ref> In 2002, Grasim would increase its stake in L&T to 15% and its attempt to launch an open offer to acquire an additional 20% stake was stayed by the [[Securities and Exchange Board of India|SEBI]] over a possible violation of takeover rules.<ref>{{cite news |title=Grasim objects to L&T cement hive off plan |url=https://www.rediff.com/money/report/grasim/20021210.htm |access-date=8 May 2024 |work=Rediff |language=en}}</ref>

In 2003, L&T announced that it would [[Demerger|demerge]] the cement business into a company called UltraTech CemCo. As part of the demerger plan, Grasim agreed to acquire an 8.5% stake in UltraTech CemCo from L&T, make an open offer to acquire another 30%, and transfer its 15% stake in L&T (residual engineering company) to L&T Employees Welfare Foundation.<ref>{{cite news |title=Grasim to acquire L&T cement business |url=https://timesofindia.indiatimes.com/business/india-business/grasim-to-acquire-lt-cement-business/articleshow/27685.cms |access-date=8 May 2024 |work=The Times of India |date=17 June 2003}}</ref><ref>{{cite news |title=L&T set for cement demerger |url=https://economictimes.indiatimes.com/business-empires-the-birlas/av-birla-group/ultra-tech-cemco/lt-set-for-cement-demerger/articleshow/907734.cms |access-date=8 May 2024 |work=The Economic Times |date=4 February 2004}}</ref> The deal was executed in 2004, with Grasim obtaining management control of UltraTech CemCo (later renamed as UltraTech Cement) with its 51% stake,<ref>{{cite news |title=AV Birla group to rename UltraTech Cemco |url=https://www.business-standard.com/article/companies/av-birla-group-to-rename-ultratech-cemco-104091001068_1.html |access-date=8 May 2024 |work=Business Standard}}</ref> while L&T retained 11.5% shareholding.<ref>{{cite news |title=Finally, L&T calls it quits with UltraTech |url=https://economictimes.indiatimes.com/industry/indl-goods/svs/cement/finally-lt-calls-it-quits-with-ultratech/articleshow/4642321.cms |access-date=8 May 2024 |work=The Economic Times |date=11 June 2009}}</ref>

== Mergers and acquisitions ==
2013 - Acquired [[Jaypee Group]]'s Gujarat cement unit for {{INR}}3,800 cr.<ref>{{Cite web |date=11 September 2013 |title=UltraTech acquires Jaypee Cement unit for Rs. 3,800 cr |url=https://www.hindustantimes.com/business/ultratech-acquires-jaypee-cement-unit-for-rs-3-800-cr/story-4RyHojaPqDACPjjeRhVt8H.html |access-date=4 March 2021 |website=Hindustan Times |language=en}}</ref>

2017 - Acquired [[Jaiprakash Associates]]'s six integrated cement plants for {{INR}}16,189 cr.<ref>{{Cite news |title=UltraTech completes acquisition of Jaiprakash group cement business |work=The Economic Times |url=https://economictimes.indiatimes.com/industry/indl-goods/svs/cement/ultratech-completes-acquisition-of-jaiprakash-group-cement-business/articleshow/59372842.cms?from=mdr |access-date=4 March 2021}}</ref>

2018 - Entered into a scheme of arrangement with Century Textile and Industries to demerge Century's cement business into ultratech.<ref>{{Cite web |last=Jain |first=Aniruddha |date=18 June 2018 |title=UltraTech acquires Century Textiles' cement business {{!}} M&A Critique |url=https://mnacritique.mergersindia.com/century-textiles-industries-demerger-ultratech-cement/ |access-date=4 March 2021 |language=en-US}}</ref>

Nov 2018 - Acquired [[Binani Cement]] for {{INR}}7,266 cr.<ref>{{Cite web |title=BCL auction: UltraTech to buy Binani Cement for Rs 7,266 crore, seeks end to insolvency proceedings |url=https://www.businesstoday.in/current/corporate/bcl-auction-ultratech-to-buy-binani-cement-for-rs-7266-crore/story/272974.html |access-date=4 March 2021 |website=businesstoday.in |date=19 March 2018}}</ref><ref>{{Cite news |last=Gaur |first=Vatsala |title=Ultratech Cement makes Binani its subsidiary |work=The Economic Times |url=https://economictimes.indiatimes.com/industry/indl-goods/svs/cement/ultratech-cement-makes-binani-its-subsidiary/articleshow/66708386.cms?from=mdr |access-date=4 March 2021}}</ref>

Dec 2023 - Acquired Cement grinding assets of Burnpur Cement Ltd. From [[Punjab National Bank]]'s Asset Reconstruction Company's auction for cash consideration of {{INRConvert|169.79|c}}.<ref>{{Cite web|url=https://www.financialexpress.com/business/industry-ultratech-cement-acquires-cement-grinding-assets-of-burnpur-cement-for-rs-169-79-crore-3321051/|title=Ultratech Cement acquires cement grinding assets of burnpur cement|date=29 November 2023 }}</ref>

Dec 2024 - Acquired majority stake in [[India Cements]] for {{INR}}7096.35 cr.<ref>{{Cite news |date=2024-12-20 |title=CCI approves Ultratech Cement's acquisition of India Cements |url=https://economictimes.indiatimes.com/industry/indl-goods/svs/cement/cci-approves-ultratech-cements-acquistion-of-india-cements/articleshow/116505709.cms?from=mdr |access-date=2025-11-04 |work=The Economic Times |issn=0013-0389}}</ref><ref>{{Cite web |last=Standard |first=Business |title=New leadership for India Cements, UltraTech appoints new CEO & CFO for new subsidiary |url=https://www.business-standard.com/companies/news/new-leadership-for-india-cements-ultratech-appoints-new-ceo-cfo-for-new-subsidiary-125010100301_1.html |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20250123101543/https://www.business-standard.com/companies/news/new-leadership-for-india-cements-ultratech-appoints-new-ceo-cfo-for-new-subsidiary-125010100301_1.html |archive-date=2025-01-23 |access-date=2025-11-04 |website=www.business-standard.com |language=en-US}}</ref>

== Controversies==
In January 2022, one worker died and two others were injured in the company's plant at [[Jafrabad]], [[Gujarat]], after hot liquid raw material fell on them while cleaning a silo during a plant shutdown.<ref>{{cite news |title=Worker killed at UltraTech Cement’s Jafrabad plant in Gujarat |url=https://www.globalcement.com/news/item/13618-worker-killed-at-ultratech-cement-s-jafrabad-plant-in-gujarat |access-date=16 August 2025 |work=Global Cement |date=2 February 2022}}</ref>

In July 2023, three workers died in an oxygen cylinder explosion at UltraTech Cement's plant in Hirmi, [[Chhattisgarh]].<ref>{{cite news |title=3 Workers Killed In Cylinder Blast At Chhattisgarh Cement Factory |url=https://www.ndtv.com/india-news/3-workers-killed-in-cylinder-blast-at-chhattisgarh-cement-factory-4219136 |access-date=16 August 2025 |work=NDTV |date=19 July 2023}}</ref> In June 2024, a worker died after getting trapped in the belt of a machine at the [[Manawar]] factory in [[Madhya Pradesh]].<ref>{{cite news |title=Labourer dies in MP cement plant; mob ransacks factory premises, damages vehicles |url=https://www.telegraphindia.com/india/labourer-dies-in-mp-cement-plant-mob-ransacks-factory-premises-damages-vehicles/cid/2027756 |access-date=16 August 2025 |work=The Telegraph |language=en}}</ref>

In July 2024, three workers died and 13 suffered burn injuries after hot [[Mortar (masonry)|mortar]] fell on them due to a boiler explosion at the company's factory near [[Jaggayyapeta]], [[Andhra Pradesh]], prompting the state government to issue a closure notice to the factory pending conclusion of an investigation.<ref>{{cite news |title=Toll in cement factory accident rises to three |url=https://timesofindia.indiatimes.com/city/vijayawada/three-dead-in-cement-factory-accident/articleshow/111701435.cms |access-date=16 August 2025 |work=The Times of India |date=13 July 2024}}</ref>
